prompt: `pg-0` was deleted, and the new `pg-0` still had the `orders` table. Why?

choices.text: PostgreSQL copied it from a replica
choices.why: There was only one copy.

choices.text: The StatefulSet backed it up before deleting
choices.why: A StatefulSet takes no backups.

choices.text: The new pod mounted the same claim
choices.why: Right. The claim belongs to the name `pg-0`, not to the pod.
An `emptyDir` dies with its pod.

prompt: What does `clusterIP: None` give the `pg` Service?
hint: How did the backup Job reach the database?

choices.text: A DNS name per pod, such as `pg-0.pg`
choices.why: Right. A headless Service resolves straight to the pods.
That is a NodePort or LoadBalancer.
A Service does not encrypt anything.
The StatefulSet names it in `serviceName`.

prompt: A StatefulSet with `volumeClaimTemplates` is deleted by mistake. With the default settings, what happens to the claims?
hint: Losing a database to a typo is the risk being avoided.

choices.why: Only if the retention policy says so.

choices.text: They move to the default namespace
choices.why: Claims never change namespace.
Nothing converts a claim.
Right, and a new StatefulSet with the same name mounts them again.

prompt: Which of these does the volume behind `data-pg-0` NOT protect against?
hint: The volume holds the database's current files.

choices.why: The capture showed the data survive that.
Right. The volume faithfully keeps the dropped state; only a copy elsewhere brings it back.
The pod and its volume stay.

choices.text: A rolling update of the StatefulSet
choices.why: The new pod mounts the same claim.

prompt: Why did the manifest raise `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` to 60?
hint: What happens when the grace period runs out?

choices.why: A longer grace period can only make it slower.

choices.text: PostgreSQL refuses to start without it
choices.why: It starts with the default too.

choices.text: To let a checkpoint finish before SIGKILL
choices.why: Right. A killed database starts slower, recovering from its log.

choices.text: To give the backup Job time to run
choices.why: The Job is separate from the pod's shutdown.

prompt: A team on one cloud wants daily backups, a standby replica and automatic failover with the least work. What does the lesson recommend?
hint: Who runs failover in each column of the table?

choices.why: A StatefulSet does no failover or backups.
Right. Those come as settings there.

choices.text: A CronJob running `pg_dump` and nothing else
choices.why: That covers backups only.

choices.text: An `emptyDir` with a large size limit
choices.why: It dies with the pod.
